newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan holds 11 police for Bhutto brother death.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan holds 11 police for Bhutto brother death.

text.p: Pakistani police said on Thursday they had arrested 11 policemen in connection with the killing of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza.

Bhutto has said Murtaza's killing along with seven followers in a police shootout on September 20 near his home in Karachi was a political murder and part of a conspiracy against her government and family.
But she has not specified people responsible for the alleged conspiracy while a judicial commission is inquiring into the incident.

A Sindh province police statement said the seven policemen -- an assistant sub-inspector, two head constables and eight constables -- were arrested on accusations lodged by a personal servant of Murtaza who was witness to the shooting.
Further investigations are in progress, it said, without giving any details.

Murtaza's breakaway Shaheed Bhutto faction of the ruling Pakistan People's Party has boycotted the judicial inquiry and demanded that senior police officials should be arrested for the alleged murder.
It was not immediately known whether the faction would be satisfied with Thursday's arrests of junior police officials.

Murtaza returned to Pakistan in 1993 after about 17 years of self-imposed exile, mostly in Syria, since his father Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was toppled as prime minister in a 1977 army coup He was executed in 1979 on a controversial conviction for conspiring to commit a political murder.

The arrest of the police officials was announced on the eve of the mourning Chehlum ceremony for Murtaza at his home town of Larkana where his Lebanese-born wife is likely to take over the leadership of his political group.
